title: SRE weekly ops sync notes - 2026-03-11 (draft)
content:
Purpose: prep notes + follow-ups for weekly SRE ops sync (Wed 11:00). Informal - things to surface for reliability review and quick decisions.

Context / TL;DR:
- SLO trends: API availability slipping toward 99.85% for the last 7 days (target 99.9%). Latency P95 increased from ~140ms to ~220ms across traffic spike windows.
- Paging: on-call pages increased this sprint (avg 6/day -> 8/day last 7d). Noise from rate-limit and healthcheck storms.
- Top incidents: 1) 2026-03-08 KV-cache eviction cascade -> sustained latency; 2) 2026-03-10 us-west-2 network blips -> elevated 5xxs and failovers. Both have partial mitigations; final fixes in progress.

Agenda items (quick):
1) SLO review (metrics + immediate mitigations) - Ravi (5m)
2) Paging noise root causes + alert tuning plan - Lina (10m)
3) Incident updates + rollforward timeline (cache fix + network retries) - Maya + infra (10m)
4) Product ask: relax strict retry on client side for streaming endpoints (PM follow-up) - Jamie (5m)
5) Action items recap and owners (5m)

SLOs / Metrics to show in meeting:
- API availability (30d / 7d / 24h) with error budget burn. Current: 7d availability ~99.85% (error budget usage ~65% for next 30d if trend continues).
- P95 latency (tokens out): baseline 140ms, current 7d rolling 220ms during 18:00-20:00 UTC window.
- Successful streaming sessions %: 98.6% (target 99.5%).
- Paging rate (pages per day) last 7 days: [9,7,6,8,10,9,8] avg 8.1.

Paging trends / noise analysis (notes):
- Biggest source: rate-limit alerts triggered by exponential client retries from <partner-integration>. Pattern: client retry storms after transient 429s -> cascading.
- Healthcheck floods from a misconfigured kubeprober on canary nodes produced ~3500 health pings -> autoscaling thrash + increased CPU -> more latency.
- Alert volume has high duplication: Prometheus alert rule fires for both service-level and instance-level. Need de-dup + grouping in pagerduty.

Top incidents (summary + current state):
1) Incident: kv-cache eviction cascade (2026-03-08)\n   - Symptom: sudden P95 jump, 5xx spikes across model-serving pods; KV cache miss ratio up x10; sustained CPU increase.\n   - Root cause (current working hypothesis): eviction algorithm threshold too low for sustained prefix-heavy workload; compaction job overlapped with peak traffic leading to mass invalidations.\n   - Immediate mitigation: rollback compaction change + increased cache memory pool (rolled 2026-03-09 02:30) - reduced P95 by ~30% but not down to baseline.\n   - Final fix: cache eviction algorithm patch merged (GIT-PR-5123) -> needs canary deploy and monitoring (Ravi).\n   - PMR status: draft complete, awaiting metrics appendix.

2) Incident: us-west-2 network flaps (2026-03-10)
   - Symptom: elevated 502/503 between 03:00-04:30 UTC, auto-failover triggered, some clients saw connection resets.
   - Root cause: provider-side network maintenance + our BGP route convergence was slow due to small routing table TTL config.
   - Mitigations: emergency traffic redistribution to us-west-1 (manual), increased connection retry backoff on client side for streaming.
   - Final fix: provider confirmed follow-up; infra will add routing TTL change + improve failover automation (Maya own).

Open risks / asks before meeting:
- If SLO keeps trending down, we should consider temporarily raising quota for Dedicated customers to move heavy tails to dedicated pools. Ops needs quick approval path from PM/Revenue.
- We need to tune rate-limit thresholds with product for partner integrations that have heavy backoff patterns.

Draft action items (owner / due):
- Ravi: Canary deploy cache eviction fix to 10% of serving fleet, monitor P95 and cache hit ratio. Due: 2026-03-13.
- Lina: Consolidate duplicate Prometheus alerts and update PagerDuty grouping rules to reduce duplicate pages by 50%. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Maya: Implement routing TTL change + automated failover doc and runbook. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Jamie: Coordinate with Product (PM-REQ-78) to update client retry guidance for streaming endpoints and draft partner communication. Due: 2026-03-14.
- On-call: run a short chaos test in staging for cache compaction overlapping with peak load to validate fix. Owner: SRE oncall (linked ticket JIRA-SREP-430). Due: 2026-03-15.

Notes to raise in ops sync (explicit asks):
- Approve accelerated canary for cache fix (Ravi): risk assessment ready in PR comments.
- Approve temporary quota bump process for Dedicated customers (ops ask to PM / RevOps).
- Confirm timeline from infra for routing TTL change and automation (Maya).

Loose ideas / backlog (follow-ups to capture):
- Improve prefix KV cache observability: add per-key TTL histograms, and noise-resistant alerts.
- Add a circuit-breaker layer at gateway to stop client retry storms from hitting serving fleet.
- 1-week pilot of stricter rate-limits + partner whitelisting for high-volume integrations.

Quick links to call out in meeting:
- SLO dashboard: CONFLUENCE-6624
- Cache fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/5123
- Related incident PMR (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pmr/kv-cache-2026-03-08
- PagerDuty escalation policy: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/escalation_policies/ops

Anything else to add?
- If no objections, I'll push this as the meeting doc and ask Lina to present paging noise section.

Quick personal notes:
- Bring numbers for error budget burn visualization (7d vs 30d).
- Keep the meeting to 30 min; follow-ups assigned as JIRA tasks post-meeting.
